maria: Heads-up — provisioning in ap-northeast1 started stalling at 08:22 UTC. Several GPU pods stuck in Pending, and our OTel metrics for that region dropped to 0. Traffic hasn't failed over automatically.
jon: On it. Can you paste the last lines from the provisioner logs and the autoscaler events? Also which routing policy was in effect for this tenant pool?
maria: Provisioner logs (tail):
```
2026-03-18T08:21:54Z provisioner: request accepted id=rr-7c2
2026-03-18T08:22:11Z k8s: failed to bind pod: Insufficient GPUs
2026-03-18T08:22:11Z provisioner: retrying allocation
2026-03-18T08:23:03Z otel-exporter: drop: export queue full
2026-03-18T08:23:03Z otel-collector: OOMKilled
```
I noticed the `otel-collector` pod for ap-northeast1 restarted around the same time.
anya: That's consistent with traces being missing. Our sampled traces from that region show gaps starting 08:22. No request IDs in the ingress logs either (they were being stripped upstream?).
liam: Router config shows primary=ap-northeast1, secondary=ap-southeast1, fallback=us-east1. Failover policy is `degraded->manual` for that capacity tier (we don't have auto-shift enabled for these reserved pools). That explains traffic still hitting ap-northeast1.
rachel: deploy-bot: otel-collector v2.14.1 deployed to ap-northeast1 at 08:25 UTC (rolling), but I see crash loops on a few nodes.
jon: Can someone run `kubectl -n infra get pods -l app=otel-collector -o wide` and `kubectl describe pod <pod>` for a crashed one? Also check node allocatable GPUs and kube-scheduler events.
maria: Ran checks:
```
NAME                            READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   NODE
otel-collector-0                0/1     CrashLoop 5          node-az1
otel-collector-1                1/1     Running   0          node-az2
```
describe shows `OOMKilled` and memory spike to ~3.2Gi. Current mem limit was 2Gi.
liam: Looks like a recent config change increased exporter batching and queue size (to improve throughput) but we didn't bump collector memory. Combined with GPU provisioning hot path causing more telemetry, collector hit OOM and blocked, exporter queue backpressure made provisioner log drop metrics and slow.
anya: That explains instrumentation gap. Critical gap: when collector fails we have no fallback path for DM metrics (we rely solely on collector -> exporter pipeline). We should add a synthetic heartbeat metric pushed to Prometheus Pushgateway from the provisioner as fallback, and add a small local buffer to exporter (filesystem-backed queue) in case of transient outages.
jon: Short-term mitigation: 1) Increase otel-collector mem limit to 4Gi and restart the pods. 2) Temporarily reduce exporter batch size so memory usage drops. 3) Manually shift traffic off ap-northeast1 to us-east1 for the reserved pools until capacity stabilizes.
maria: I'm bumping mem and rolling the collector now. Command:
```
kubectl -n infra set resources deployment/otel-collector --limits=memory=4Gi
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/otel-collector
```
liam: I'll open a routing change to shift impacted customer pools to us-east1. Expect 3–5 min to propagate.
rachel: Quick note: shifting to us-east will increase cost ~2x for those requests due to cross-region egress and larger instance sizes. We should notify CS for impacted customers.
jon: Also add this to the incident runbook: if otel-collector OOMs, auto-scale mem to +2x and reduce batch size automatically. We missed that automation.
anya: Ops-level follow-up (short-term): implement a tiny pushgateway client in provisioner to emit `provisioner_heartbeat{region="ap-northeast1"}=1` every 10s, with TTL 30s. Long-term: make exporter resilience configurable with filesystem queue and backpressure signals.
maria: Post-change: collector restarted and memory stable on node-az2; otel metrics started showing up again at 08:34 UTC. Provisioner recovered allocation retries and several Pending pods bound.
liam: Router shift completed at 08:38 UTC; traffic to affected reserved pools is on us-east1. No errors in router logs during shift, latency increased ~80ms for affected customers.
rachel: CS notified with estimated cost delta and expected recovery timeline.
